candidate.derivedAnswer: B, approximately $83.33 per month; exactly 250/3 dollars
candidate.answerReason: The annual net profit is $550. After the repair allowance, annual rent must cover $550+$325=$875. This is 87.5% of annual rent, so annual rent is $1000 and monthly rent is $1000/12≈$83.33.

methods.label: Work backward from the annual profit
methods.explanation:
Put all amounts on a yearly basis. The required annual profit after the repair allowance and taxes is
\[
0.055\cdot10{,}000=550\text{ dollars}.
\]
Reserving \(12\tfrac12\%\) of each month's rent also reserves that percentage of the year's rent. The remaining \(87\tfrac12\%=0.875\) must cover both the profit and the annual taxes, totaling
\[
550+325=875\text{ dollars}.
\]
Because \(875\) dollars is only \(87.5\%\) of the annual rent, divide by \(0.875\) to recover the whole:
\[
\text{annual rent}=\frac{875}{0.875}=1000\text{ dollars}.
\]
The monthly rent is therefore
\[
\frac{1000}{12}=\frac{250}{3}\approx83.33\text{ dollars}.
\]
Rounded to the nearest cent, the answer is \(\boxed{\$83.33}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: Forward percentage calculation and division to recover a whole from its known percentage are sufficient.

candidate.annotationRationale: The central target is recovering gross rent from the amount left after a percentage allowance. Forward percentage calculation finds the required profit, while the known-part-to-whole division relationship supports recovering annual rent.
limitations: Choice B is rounded to the nearest cent; the exact monthly rent is 250/3 dollars.
